title: The Invisible Gap: Romanized Indic Generation Fails Where Automatic Metrics Succeed
abstract: arXiv:2611.09085v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Hundreds of millions of Indians communicate with digital systems in romanized Latin characters -- typing "aap kaise hain" rather than native script -- yet romanized Indic generation is absent from NLP benchmarks and evaluation frameworks. We demonstrate that automatic metrics (BGE-M3, BERTScore) systematically misrepresent the quality of romanized Hindi, Telugu, and Kannada generation. We evaluate four LLMs (Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Gemini 2.5-flash, Qwen3.5-35B) on 142 OpenAssistant query-response pairs. On a 72-response diagnostic subset, native speakers rate GPT-5.5 1.43 points higher than Claude Opus 4.8 on a 12-point rubric, whereas their full-dataset BGE-M3 means differ by only 0.004. Two distinct model-specific failure modes emerge: Gemini produces script spillage (16.9% of Telugu responses leak native script), while Qwen collapses to English-only output (16.2% of Kannada responses). We introduce a failure-aware evaluation policy

translated_title: 隐形的鸿沟：自动指标看好之处，罗马化印度语言生成实则失败
translated_abstract: 数亿印度人使用罗马化拉丁字母与数字系统交流——例如输入"aap kaise hain"而非天城文等原生文字——然而罗马化印度语言的生成在NLP基准测试与评估框架中却付之阙如。我们证明自动指标（BGE-M3、BERTScore）会系统性地误报罗马化印地语、泰卢固语和卡纳达语生成的质量。我们在142个OpenAssistant问答对上评估了四个大语言模型（Claude Opus 4.8、GPT-5.5、Gemini 2.5-flash、Qwen3.5-35B）。在一个包含72条回复的诊断子集上，母语者在12分评分量表上给GPT-5.5的评分比Claude Opus 4.8高出1.43分，而两者在全数据集上的BGE-M3均值差异仅为0.004。研究揭示出两种截然不同的模型特定失败模式：Gemini产生文字溢出（16.9%的泰卢固语回复泄漏出原生文字），而Qwen则退化为纯英文输出（16.2%的卡纳达语回复）。我们提出了一种故障感知的评估策略。
tldr: 该研究发现自动指标（如BGE-M3）系统性地误报罗马化印度语言生成的真实质量——人类评分差距显著而指标差异近乎为零，并揭示出文字溢出与英文退化两种模型失败模式，据此提出故障感知的评估策略。
en_tdlr: Automatic metrics like BGE-M3 systematically misrepresent the quality of romanized Indic generation—masking large human-rated gaps and model-specific failures such as script spillage and English collapse—motivating a failure-aware evaluation policy.
